name: Eridu

name: Uruk

name: Ur

name: Lagash

name: Girsu

name: Nippur

name: Kish

name: Umma

name: Shuruppak

name: Isin

name: Larsa

name: Sippar

name: Borsippa

name: Babylon

name: Akkad

name: Eshnunna

name: Adab

name: Kutha

name: Dilbat

name: Marad

name: Zabalam

name: Bad-tibira

name: Larak

name: Akshak

name: Mashkan-shapir

name: Tell es-Sawwan

name: Jarmo

name: Tell Halaf

name: Qana
summary: Hadrami port of the Periplus shipping incense to Egypt and India.

name: Najran
summary: Caravan oasis and Christian centre martyred under the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas.

name: Zafar
summary: Highland capital of Himyar, which unified Yemen and adopted monotheism.

name: Sana'a
summary: Highland capital of tower houses, seat of Yemeni states from Himyar onward.

name: Aden
summary: Volcanic-crater harbour controlling the Red Sea entrance for Indian Ocean trade.

name: Zabid
summary: Tihama city whose university spread Islamic learning and algebra in Yemen.

name: Shibam
summary: Mudbrick high-rise city, the earliest example of vertical urban planning.

name: Tarim
summary: Hadrami centre of Sufi scholarship that seeded Islam across the Indian Ocean.

name: Nabta Playa
summary: Seasonal cattle-herder camp with megalithic calendar circles; ceremonial, not a city.

name: Merimde Beni Salama
summary: Large Delta Neolithic village, one of Egypt's first substantial settlements; not a city.

name: Hierakonpolis
summary: Predynastic capital where kingship took shape; source of the Narmer palette.

name: Naqada
summary: Predynastic centre that named the culture out of which pharaonic Egypt emerged.

name: Abydos
summary: Royal cemetery of Egypt's first kings and the great cult centre of Osiris.

name: Thinis
summary: Traditional home of the Thinite kings who unified Egypt; site not securely located.

name: Buto
summary: Predynastic Lower Egyptian capital of the cobra goddess Wadjet.

name: Sais
summary: Delta cult city of Neith and capital of the 26th Dynasty renaissance.

name: Memphis
summary: Egypt's founding capital at the Delta apex, administrative heart for three millennia.

name: Heit el-Ghurab
summary: Barracks and bakery town that housed pyramid builders; a support settlement, not a city.

name: Saqqara
summary: Memphis's vast necropolis with the first pyramid; a cemetery complex, not a city.

name: Heliopolis
summary: Solar theology's home city, its priesthood shaping Egyptian religion and obelisks.

name: Herakleopolis Magna
summary: Rival capital to Thebes during Egypt's first collapse.

name: Hermopolis Magna
summary: Cult city of Thoth and of the Ogdoad creation myth.

name: Akhetaten
summary: Akhenaten's purpose-built monotheist capital, occupied barely two decades.

name: Lycopolis
summary: Upper Egyptian nome capital and later a major Coptic centre.

name: Akhmim
summary: Cult city of Min and a famous weaving town into Islamic times.

name: Dendera
summary: Temple city of Hathor with a near-complete Ptolemaic temple and zodiac ceiling.

name: Coptos
summary: Desert-road hub linking the Nile to Red Sea ports and the Eastern Desert quarries.

name: Thebes
summary: Imperial and religious capital of New Kingdom Egypt, home of Karnak and the royal valleys.

name: Deir el-Medina
summary: Village of the tomb-builders whose records reveal daily life and the first strike; not a city.

name: Elkab
summary: Walled cult city of the vulture goddess Nekhbet, twin of Hierakonpolis.

name: Edfu
summary: Home of Egypt's best-preserved temple, dedicated to Horus.

name: Esna
summary: Nile temple town of the god Khnum.

name: Ombos
summary: Double temple town shared between Sobek and Horus.

name: Elephantine
summary: Island fortress and trade gateway to Nubia, home to a Jewish garrison and its Aramaic papyri.

name: Syene
summary: Granite quarry city where Eratosthenes measured the earth.

name: Avaris
summary: Hyksos capital in the eastern Delta, with Levantine and Aegean-style palaces.

name: Pi-Ramesses
summary: Ramesses II's Delta capital and chariot-manufacturing city, abandoned as the branch silted.

name: Tanis
summary: Delta capital built from Pi-Ramesses' stones, with intact silver royal burials.

name: Bubastis
summary: Cat-goddess festival city and Libyan-dynasty capital.

name: Mendes
summary: Delta ram-cult city and briefly a Late Period capital.

name: Athribis
summary: Delta nome capital, birthplace of a 30th Dynasty line.

name: Leontopolis
summary: Delta lion-cult city and seat of a rival Libyan dynasty.

name: Naukratis
summary: Greek treaty port in the Delta, Egypt's controlled window on Aegean trade.

name: Thonis-Heracleion
summary: Egypt's Mediterranean customs port, now submerged after subsidence.

name: Canopus
summary: Pleasure and temple city at the Nile's western mouth, partly underwater.

name: Pelusium
summary: Fortress port guarding Egypt's eastern gate, silted up and abandoned.

name: Alexandria
summary: Ptolemaic capital of the Library, Lighthouse and Mediterranean learning.

name: Crocodilopolis
summary: Faiyum capital at the centre of Egypt's greatest reclamation scheme.

name: Kahun
summary: Planned pyramid-workers' town, the best-preserved Middle Kingdom settlement plan; not a city.

name: Oxyrhynchus
summary: Provincial capital whose rubbish mounds yielded the largest ancient papyrus haul.

name: Antinoöpolis
summary: Hadrian's Greek foundation commemorating Antinous's drowning.

name: Kellis
summary: Desert oasis town preserving Manichaean and Christian papyri, abandoned to the sand.

name: Siwa
summary: Oracle oasis of Amun consulted by Alexander.

name: Bahariya
summary: Wine-producing oasis with a vast Greco-Roman gilded-mummy cemetery.

name: Berenike Troglodytica
summary: Ptolemaic elephant and Roman Indian Ocean port on the Red Sea.

name: Myos Hormos
summary: Chief Roman Red Sea harbour for the Indian trade.

name: Fustat
summary: Arab garrison city that became Egypt's Islamic capital and glass-and-ceramic hub, absorbed into Cairo.

name: Cairo
summary: Fatimid royal foundation that grew into the largest city of the medieval Islamic world.

name: Al-Askar and Al-Qata'i
summary: Successive Abbasid and Tulunid palace-cities north of Fustat, later merged into Cairo.

name: Damietta
summary: Delta port and Crusader target controlling the eastern Nile mouth.

name: Rosetta
summary: Western Nile mouth port, later namesake of the trilingual stone.

name: Qus
summary: Mamluk-era Nile city and staging point for the Red Sea spice route.

name: Aydhab
summary: Red Sea pilgrim and spice port, destroyed by the Mamluks.

name: Kerma
summary: First Nubian kingdom's capital, with the huge mudbrick Western Deffufa.

name: Buhen
summary: Egyptian fortress town at the second cataract, now under Lake Nasser.

name: Mirgissa
summary: Middle Kingdom fortress and trans-shipment depot with a boat slipway; a fort, not a city.

name: Semna
summary: Frontier fortress controlling Nubian trade and Nile levels; a fort, not a city.

name: Sai
summary: Egyptian colonial town on a Nile island, later a Christian Nubian centre.

name: Sesebi
summary: Planned Egyptian walled colonial town in Nubia.

name: Napata
summary: Kushite religious capital under Jebel Barkal, whence the 25th Dynasty conquered Egypt.

name: Nuri
summary: Kushite royal pyramid cemetery near Napata; a necropolis, not a city.

name: Kawa
summary: Kushite temple town of Amun, rebuilt by Taharqa.

name: Meroë
summary: Iron-smelting Kushite capital with hundreds of pyramids and its own Meroitic script.

name: Naqa
summary: Meroitic temple city of Amun and the lion god Apedemak.

name: Musawwarat es-Sufra
summary: Meroitic pilgrimage complex of the Great Enclosure; ceremonial, not a city.

name: Qasr Ibrim
summary: Cliff fortress-town, the only major Nubian site above the reservoir, with vast preserved documents.

name: Faras
summary: Capital of Christian Nobadia, whose cathedral frescoes were rescued before flooding.

name: Old Dongola
summary: Capital of Christian Makuria that held off Arab armies for six centuries.

name: Soba
summary: Capital of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alwa on the Blue Nile.

name: Yeha
summary: Capital of the D'mt polity with a monumental Sabaean-style temple, Ethiopia's oldest standing building.

name: Aksum
summary: Capital of an Indian Ocean trading empire that minted coins, raised stelae and adopted Christianity early.

name: Adulis
summary: Aksum's Red Sea port, hub of ivory and incense trade with Rome and India.

name: Matara
summary: Pre-Aksumite and Aksumite inland town on the route from Adulis to Aksum.

name: Qohaito
summary: Aksumite highland town identified with Coloe, a stop on the ivory road.

name: Lalibela
summary: Zagwe capital of eleven rock-hewn churches, conceived as a new Jerusalem.

name: Harar
summary: Walled Islamic city of the Horn, a centre of trade, learning and coffee.

name: Zeila
summary: Red Sea port and gateway for Islam into the Ethiopian interior.

name: Mogadishu
summary: Leading Somali coast city-state trading gold, ivory and cloth across the Indian Ocean.

name: Carthage
summary: Phoenician sea empire's capital, Rome's great rival, refounded as a Roman metropolis.

name: Utica
summary: Oldest Phoenician colony in Africa, later a Roman city stranded by silting.

name: Hadrumetum
summary: Phoenician then Roman port at the heart of the olive-oil economy.

name: Thapsus
summary: Punic port where Caesar crushed the Pompeians in Africa.

name: Kerkouane
summary: Punic town abandoned and never rebuilt, so preserving pure Carthaginian domestic architecture.

name: Thugga
summary: Numidian then Roman hill city with a Libyco-Punic mausoleum and a fine theatre.

name: Thysdrus
summary: Olive-boom city that built Africa's greatest amphitheatre.

name: Sufetula
summary: Roman olive city with a triple-temple forum, briefly a Byzantine African capital.

name: Cirta
summary: Numidian royal capital of Massinissa on a gorge plateau.

name: Hippo Regius
summary: Numidian port and Augustine's bishopric, key to Latin Christian thought.

name: Iol Caesarea
summary: Punic port made Juba II's Hellenistic royal capital of Mauretania.

name: Tipasa
summary: Punic-Roman coastal town with major early Christian basilicas.

name: Thamugadi
summary: Trajan's perfectly gridded veteran colony, abandoned and buried by sand.

name: Lambaesis
summary: Legionary fortress-city headquarters of Rome's African army.

name: Cuicul
summary: Mountain colony with exceptionally preserved Roman streets and mosaics.

name: Tahert
summary: Capital of the Rustamid Ibadi imamate, a trans-Saharan trade node.

name: Qal'at Bani Hammad
summary: Hammadid mountain capital abandoned after Almohad conquest.

name: Ashir
summary: Early Zirid fortified capital in the Algerian highlands.

name: Bejaia
summary: Hammadid port that transmitted Arabic numerals to Europe through Fibonacci.

name: Tlemcen
summary: Zayyanid capital and northern terminus of the Sijilmasa gold road.

name: Oea
summary: Phoenician member of the Tripolis and the surviving one of the three.

name: Leptis Magna
summary: Punic port lavishly rebuilt by its native son Septimius Severus, then lost to sand.

name: Sabratha
summary: Tripolitanian port of the Saharan trade with a monumental seaside theatre.

name: Cyrene
summary: Greek colony that became the intellectual capital of Libya, home of Eratosthenes.

name: Apollonia
summary: Cyrene's harbour, later capital of Byzantine Libya, now partly submerged.

name: Ptolemais
summary: Pentapolis city with grand cisterns that became the Roman provincial seat.

name: Barca
summary: Cyrenaican inland city, later the region's Islamic administrative centre.

name: Berenice
summary: Pentapolis port refounded by the Ptolemies, ancestor of Benghazi.

name: Garama
summary: Garamantian capital in the Sahara sustained by foggara tunnel irrigation.

name: Ghadames
summary: Saharan caravan oasis of covered streets, a Roman outpost then a trade hub.

name: Ghat
summary: Tuareg Saharan caravan town on the route to Kano and Timbuktu.

name: Kairouan
summary: First great Islamic city of the Maghreb and base for the conquest of Iberia.

name: Mahdia
summary: Fortified peninsula capital founded by the first Fatimid caliph.

name: Tunis
summary: Punic town that replaced Carthage as the region's capital under the Hafsids.

name: Raqqada
summary: Aghlabid and early Fatimid palace-city outside Kairouan.

name: Volubilis
summary: Mauretanian and Roman city of olive presses and mosaics, later Idrisid base.

name: Lixus
summary: Phoenician Atlantic colony making purple dye and salt fish.

name: Mogador
summary: Atlantic island trading post for purple dye at the edge of the known world.

name: Tingis
summary: Strait of Gibraltar port and capital of Mauretania Tingitana.

name: Sala Colonia
summary: Southernmost Roman Atlantic city, later a Marinid necropolis.

name: Ceuta
summary: Strait fortress-port and Mediterranean gateway of the Maghreb.

name: Fez
summary: Idrisid foundation that became the Maghreb's intellectual capital with the Qarawiyyin.

name: Marrakesh
summary: Almoravid then Almohad imperial capital and northern gate of the Sahara trade.

name: Meknes
summary: Berber town that grew into an imperial Moroccan capital.

name: Aghmat
summary: Pre-Almoravid capital of the Marrakesh plain, eclipsed by its neighbour.

name: Sijilmasa
summary: Northern terminus of the Saharan gold road, minting the dinars that funded Mediterranean trade.

name: Rabat
summary: Almohad fortified camp-city built as a springboard for Iberian campaigns.

name: Dhar Tichitt
summary: Dry-stone settlement cluster, West Africa's earliest known urbanising complex.

name: Awdaghost
summary: Berber-Soninke caravan city where Saharan salt met Sahelian gold.

name: Kumbi Saleh
summary: Probable capital of the Ghana empire, a twin city of merchants and kings.
contested: Identification as Ghana's capital is probable but not certain.

name: Walata
summary: Saharan caravan and scholarly town on the Timbuktu route.

name: Djenné-Djenno
summary: Africa's oldest known city south of the Sahara, built without centralised kingship.

name: Djenné
summary: Inland Niger Delta trade and scholarship city of great mudbrick mosques.

name: Dia
summary: Early Middle Niger urban cluster contemporary with and older than Jenne-jeno.

name: Timbuktu
summary: Saharan port of the Niger whose madrasas and manuscript libraries made it a legend.

name: Gao
summary: Songhai imperial capital on the Niger bend, controlling the eastern gold and salt roads.

name: Tadmekka
summary: Berber-Sahelian trade town that struck unstamped gold coins.

name: Niani
summary: Traditional capital of the Mali empire under Sundiata and Mansa Musa.
contested: Identification as Mali's capital is debated.

name: Takedda
summary: Copper-producing Saharan town described by Ibn Battuta.

name: Agadez
summary: Tuareg sultanate city and southern gateway of the central Saharan routes.

name: Njimi
summary: Capital of the Kanem empire east of Lake Chad; its site remains unidentified.

name: Kano
summary: Walled Hausa city-state of indigo dyeing and the greatest Sahelian market.

name: Katsina
summary: Hausa city-state rivalling Kano for the trans-Saharan trade and Islamic learning.

name: Zazzau
summary: Hausa city-state, historically the southern slave-and-trade frontier.

name: Ile-Ife
summary: Yoruba spiritual capital that produced naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads.

name: Oyo-Ile
summary: Capital of the Oyo empire, the great Yoruba cavalry state.

name: Benin City
summary: Walled Edo capital of enormous earthworks and the Benin bronzes.

name: Igbo-Ukwu
summary: Site of astonishingly sophisticated cast bronzes and a rich burial; a ritual centre, not a city.

name: Begho
summary: Forest-edge market town where Akan gold entered the Saharan network.

name: Bono Manso
summary: Capital of the earliest Akan state, a gold and kola entrepôt.

name: Sine-Ngayene
summary: Vast megalithic burial complex of the Senegambia; ceremonial, not a city.

name: Kilwa Kisiwani
summary: Dominant Swahili sultanate, coral-stone city that monopolised the Zimbabwe gold trade.

name: Manda
summary: Early Swahili stone town trading with the Gulf and China.

name: Shanga
summary: Earliest excavated Swahili settlement with a sequence of timber-to-stone mosques.

name: Lamu
summary: Continuously inhabited Swahili stone town of the northern Kenya coast.

name: Pate
summary: Swahili city-state rival of Lamu, famed for silk weaving.

name: Gedi
summary: Prosperous Swahili coral town mysteriously abandoned in the 17th century.

name: Unguja Ukuu
summary: Early Indian Ocean trading settlement on Zanzibar, predating the Swahili stone towns.

name: Sofala
summary: Southernmost Swahili port, the outlet for Zimbabwean gold.

name: Mapungubwe
summary: First southern African class-based state capital, with gold rhinoceros burials on a sacred hill.

name: Great Zimbabwe
summary: Largest stone-built city in sub-Saharan Africa, capital of a cattle-and-gold empire.

name: Khami
summary: Successor capital to Great Zimbabwe with decorated dry-stone terraces.

name: Thulamela
summary: Stone-walled Venda-linked settlement continuing the Mapungubwe tradition.

name: Ingombe Ilede
summary: Zambezi trading settlement with gold-and-copper burials linking interior to coast.
